newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says Albanians set example to their leaders.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says Albanians set example to their leaders.

text.p: Germany said on Monday Albanians had shown their determination to return to orderly behaviour and called on politicians to follow the example set by voters.
"Albania's citizens expressed their will to return to orderly relations in an impressive way," Foreign Ministry spokesman Martin Erdmann said in a statement, referring to Sunday's general election.
"Politicians and parties of the country must now show just as great a sense of responsibility and discipline as the large majority of the country's citizens (did) on Sunday."

"All political forces of the country must now respect the electorate's vote and support the return of Albania to normality, the achievement of ordered and democratic relations and the observance of human rights," he said.

Erdmann said politicians and parliament now had to work together for national reconciliation, respect and cooperation which were key to Albania's future and essential preconditions for continued international support.

Eberhard Brecht, foreign policy spokesman for the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), agreed. "Both winners and losers must be ready to cooperate in the urgent construction of the country," Brecht said in a statement.

Albanian President Sali Berisha conceded on Monday his Democratic Party had lost the election before official results had been declared, appearing to confirm that the Socialist Party swept to victory in the poll.

Erdmann said initial assessments of international observers were that the election had proceeded in a peaceful and orderly way in most towns and communities, although there had been a few incidents and irregularities.
